meta.note: HAND-AUTHORED from the NYSED Grades 3-8 Mathematics Educator Guide. Every figure here is a published NYSED fact, not an inference -- except expectedReleasedItems, which is recorded from the extractor's own count at ingest and then hand-confirmed against the PDF. Nothing in this file is generated, and preflight reads its counts instead of holding literals of its own.
meta.releaseNote: NYSED releases a portion of each test -- 'at least 75 percent of the test questions that appeared on the tests (including all constructed-response questions) that counted toward students' scores'. Item numbering therefore has gaps, and the gaps are the withheld items. The proportion released is not constant: 2023-2025 published noticeably fewer items than 2026, so any coverage figure must be read per year and never pooled without saying so.
meta.fieldTestNote: The per-session counts below include embedded field-test questions, which do not count toward a student's score and are not distinguishable to the student. So designedItems is the number of questions a student sees, not the number that is scored.
meta.sessionNote: Two sessions administered over two days, untimed within the school day.
meta.constructedResponseReleaseNote: NYSED's own description of these releases says they include 'all constructed-response questions that counted toward students' scores'. That holds for 2023-2025, which release all ten CR items (3 one-credit, 6 two-credit, 1 three-credit -- the full design). It does NOT hold for 2026, which releases only 8 (2 one-credit, 5 two-credit, 1 three-credit). Do not present CR coverage as complete without checking the year.
meta.columnLabelNote: The item map's domain column is headed 'Cluster' in 2023, 2025 and 2026 and 'Domain' in 2024. 2024's name is the accurate one: in every year the values are domain names, not cluster descriptions. The extractor accepts either header and calls the field domainLabel.
meta.doNotComputeReleaseShare: Never publish a '% of the test released' figure. NYSED's promise is 'at least 75 percent of the test questions that counted toward students' scores' -- the denominator is SCORED items, and designedItems above includes embedded field-test items that do not count and whose number NYSED does not publish. Dividing released items by designedItems gives 63-65% for 2023-2025, which looks like NYSED breaking its own promise and is simply the wrong denominator. Report released item counts, never a share of the test.

itemNumbering.note: All multiple-choice items are numbered before all constructed-response items, across both sessions. Verified against all four item maps.

2.calculator: four-function with a square root key, or scientific

6.domainBlueprintNote: Statistics and Probability has no percent range for grade 6 because every standard in that domain is a post-test standard: it is taught in grade 6 and assessed on the grade 7 test. This is the single most consequential pacing fact in the guide for a 6th-grade teacher.

itemNumbering.note: Verified against all four item maps.

7.domainBlueprintNote: Geometry is only 2-7% of the grade 7 test because most of the grade 7 Geometry domain is post-test and is assessed on the grade 8 test instead. The Statistics and Probability weight is largely carried by grade 6 post-test standards.

itemNumbering.note: Verified against all four item maps.

8.domainBlueprintNote: Grade 8 Geometry is weighted heavily in part because five grade 7 Geometry standards are post-test and assessed here. Note that many 8th graders at this school sit the Algebra I Regents instead of this test -- RegentsAlign covers that exam.

Multiple Choice.note: Four answer choices; distractors are based on plausible missteps.

Constructed Response.note: 1-credit: final answer only is scored. 2-credit: must show work or explain. 3-credit: two or more tasks, or one more extensive problem. Exactly one 3-credit item per test.

knownDataDefects.what: The item map prints NGLS.Math.Content.NY-NY-8.EE.6, duplicating the NY- prefix.
knownDataDefects.handling: The extractor normalises it to NY-8.EE.6 and records the repair on the item rather than hiding it.

knownDataDefects.what: Some standard cells carry trailing whitespace inside the code (e.g. 'NY-8.F.1 ').

The Cluster cell is merged across NY-7.SP.1, NY-7.SP.3 and NY-7.SP.4 (one ruled cell, y=406.0 to y=455.0) and labelled 'Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.' NY-7.SP.1 belongs to a different cluster -- 'Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population' -- whose heading the guide omits entirely, along with NY-7.SP.2.
knownDataDefects.handling: Published as the guide prints it. We do not substitute the cluster we believe NYSED meant, because clusterText is presented as the guide's own wording; NY-7.SP.1's cluster is therefore wrong in our data exactly as it is wrong in the source.
